topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by setting out the learning outcomes, the multi-step mutation progression model, and the framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Sustaining proliferative signaling and evading growth suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin, and downstream signaling pathways enable cancer cells to acquire growth signal autonomy and resist growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how differentiation blocks arrest cells in proliferative progenitor-like states across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Evading apoptosis, achieving replicative immortality, and cell-autonomous growth control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells circumvent programmed cell death and replicative limits through p53 and telomerase deregulation, concluding the examination of cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how Krebs cycle mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the biological switch requiring new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and supply nutrients for sustained tumor progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms, clinical monitoring, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the metastatic cascade, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, liquid biopsy monitoring using circulating tumor cells, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on synthesizing the cancer hallmarks and revisiting the core learning outcomes.
